The generalisation adds NO new strategy class.
4.1.14 orders on four keys: score descending, then
severity multiplier, then verified open report count,
then locality name. The v0.8 tie-break used case size,
which exists for the mosquito alone and so could not
order a mixed-pest queue. The keys live outside
PriorityScore, so the calculator supplies them rather
than the container reaching back into a repository.
rank() is a Lab 4 basis-path subject.

run() is fixed: record start, fetch,
parse, persist, record outcome, publish event, and on
failure mark the source stale (10.2.2) without losing
stored data (10.2.4). The three sources differ only in
method per driver and never named one — this was open
item 1 from Lab 2. A strategy per driver settles it as a
design decision rather than a constant buried in the
engine, and 10.6.2 already puts the weights in
The methods and parameters are now
written down in SCORING-SPEC.md §2, and the driver is a
constructor parameter rather than a constant, because
three drivers share the capped-linear method with
different caps. NormalisationFactory owns the binding and
asserts that all seven drivers of 4.1.3 resolve — two did
not, which a scoring cycle would have discovered at run
decided by the payload alone, so the Lab 4 cases run
against a 2026-09-03 fixture instead of against whatever
It exists because the feed is not shaped as the dataset
page implies: HOMES, PUBLIC_PLACES and CONSTRUCTION_SITES
are comma-separated habitat text, not counts, so 1.1.15
had to be rewritten. shouldDownload() implements the
1.1.20 metadata check that keeps the hourly cycle of
1.1.1 cheap against a feed that moves twice a week.
Table-driven state machine, deliberately not the GoF
State pattern.** State would spread eight transitions
across eight classes; the rule in 8.3.2 would then be
true of the set but visible in no single place. The table
keeps isTransitionPermitted() as one method with a
bounded branch structure — which is also what makes it
Ingestion must trigger rescoring and alert
